Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
223 PM EDT Sat Sep 19 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 222 PM EDT Saturday...

No significant changes made with this forecast package.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 222 PM EDT Saturday...

1. Light rain and cool temperatures expected on Sunday, 
followed by drier and seasonable cool weather for the start of the 
new work week.   

2. Quiet weather for the extended

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 222 PM EDT Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Sfc analysis indicates weakening 1024mb high pres 
stretching from Eastern Canada into central Maine, while  weak 
1010mb low pres is over central Iowa with warm front extending into 
the Ohio Valley. This area of low pres wl race toward the Ohio 
Valley tonight with increasing clouds acrs our fa and light rain 
developing along the warm frontal boundary by mid-morning Sunday. 
Temps drop quickly this evening, due to very dry bl conditions/light 
winds but warm after midnight. Lows generally mid 30s NEK to 
mid/upper 40s Champlain/St Lawrence Valleys. The highest pops and 
greatest qpf wl occur btwn 13z and 20z on Sunday, per best moisture 
and lift proggs. Given the lack of instability and highest pw values 
>1.30" staying south of our cwa, along with relatively quick 
movement of system, thinking qpf wl range in the 0.20" to 0.50" for 
most areas. Did note some southeast downslope component in the bl to 
900mb wind fields, which could cause some localized shadowing along 
the western slopes. In addition, RAP/HRRR sounding data at CLC 
indicates good mixing below inversion near 1000 feet of 25 to 29 
knots, so thinking a brief lake wind advisory wl be needed btwn 10z-
15z Sunday morning. As rain arrives, conditions wl stabilize and 
mixing/winds wl decrease, especially by early aftn. Next noticeable 
impact wl be the relatively cool high temps for Sunday, given 
clouds/precip. Expecting highs only mid/upper 40s mtns to mid/upper 
50s warmer valleys. A cool/raw day is anticipated with intervals of 
light rain. 

Sunday night, sounding data indicates strong subsidence inversion 
developing under caa and blocked flow. Given this synoptic scale 
scenario with rainfall in the past 6 to 12 hours, expect areas of 
low clouds/drizzle, especially favorable upslope mtn elevations 
above 1000 feet with some fog possible. Temps wl range from the mid 
30s to mid/upper 40s with no frost formation expected given the caa 
advection and bl mixing.

Monday-Tuesday...a period of very quiet wx is anticipated as strong 
1030mb high pres builds toward the International Border from Hudson 
Bay. This wl produce a cool-dry anticyclonic flow of air acrs our 
cwa, with pw values dropping <0.50". This deep dry layer wl result 
in large diurnal spread in daily temps and sharp elevation depend 
gradients from mild valleys to cool summits. Have utilized the mtn 
max temp tool to highlight this thinking, which supports highs l/m 
40s summits to upper 50s to mid 60s valleys for both Monday and 
Tuesday. Conditions look favorable for frost/freeze headlines on 
Monday night/Tuesday morning for parts of the SLV and n-central VT 
valleys. Lows generally mid/upper 20s SLK/NEK to mid/upper 30s, 
except mid 40s near Lake Champlain.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A high pressure to our north and a low pressure to our 
south will bring us several days of dry weather and cool 
temperatures, perfect for your outdoor plans. Daily highs will be in 
the 60s through Thursday before the forecast becomes less clear. 
WHile the GFS has backed off from the more extreme scenario it was 
painting during the last forecast cycle, the low pressure to  our 
south will move up the coast sometime late in the week or into the 
weekend, bringing some rain to the regions.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 18Z Sunday...VFR conditions will persist through the day
today, with scattered high clouds and light to moderate winds.
Tonight, the winds turn southeast and should remain strong enough to
keep the fog away. Tomorrow morning rain will move in. Conditions
will primarily remain VFR with some intermittent MVFR possible if
the rain showers pick up in intensity.

Outlook...

Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Monday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Thursday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
As of 222 PM EDT Saturday...

A brief Lake Wind Advisory maybe needed between 6 AM and 10 AM on 
Sunday morning for breezy south to southeast winds of 15 to 25 
knots, especially on the open waters. The winds will quickly 
decrease to 10 to 15 knots once the rain arrives and helps to 
stabilize the winds from mixing down over the warmer waters. Waves 
generally 1 to 3 feet, but localized near 4 feet possible on Sunday 
morning.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&
